title: Pixel Sprite 3D Diorama (Tilt-Shift 2.5D)
summary: A 2.5D diorama scene that places crisp pixel-art character sprites inside a lit, low-detail 3D environment with tilt-shift depth of field, bloom and volumetric light, the look popular in modern retro-inspired RPGs. Slots for location, party, time of day and palette.
prompt:
An in-game screenshot of a retro-inspired RPG that combines 2D pixel-art sprites with a 3D diorama environment.

Location: {argument name="location" default="a canal-side harbour town at dusk, stone bridges, stacked timber houses and moored fishing boats"}.
Party: {argument name="party" default="four adventurers walking in a line across a bridge: a knight, a mage in a wide hat, a scout and a small alchemist"}.
Time and weather: {argument name="time_of_day" default="blue-hour dusk with lanterns just lit and light drifting mist"}.

# Look
- Characters and NPCs are flat, front-facing pixel sprites (about 32 pixels tall, crisp nearest-neighbour pixels, limited palette) standing upright inside the 3D world, casting soft real-time shadows on the ground.
- The environment is simple 3D geometry with pixel-art textures on every surface, so it feels like a miniature model set.
- Strong tilt-shift depth of field: the band containing the party is sharp, foreground and far background melt into soft bokeh.
- Modern lighting on retro assets: warm lantern point lights with bloom, cool ambient sky light, volumetric light shafts through the mist, gentle reflections in the canal water.

# Camera and composition
- Elevated three-quarter camera at about 30 degrees, slightly zoomed like a diorama photographed from above.
- Party on the lower-third line, walking left to right toward a glowing focal landmark ({argument name="landmark" default="a lighthouse on the far pier"}).
- Clear foreground framing elements (rooftops, hanging lanterns) out of focus at the edges.

# Palette
{argument name="palette" default="deep blues and teal shadows against warm orange lantern light, small pink accents in the sky"}.

# Avoid
High-poly realistic characters, blurry or smeared sprites, mixed sprite resolutions, photographic textures, UI, dialogue boxes, text, watermarks, and any recognisable existing game characters.
